observations.claim: The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded TI up to $1.61 billion in CHIPS direct funding supporting more than $18 billion of investment through the end of the decade across two Sherman, Texas fabs and one Lehi, Utah fab; disbursement is milestone-based.

Reuters reported Q2 2026 revenue of $5.46 billion, up 23% year over year, with broad growth including industrial, data center and automotive; TI guided Q3 revenue to $5.65-$6.15 billion while shares fell more than 3% after hours.

risks.risk: Milestone-based public incentives reduce but do not eliminate execution and utilization risk from TI's large domestic capacity build.

A negative after-hours share response despite above-consensus operating results/guidance indicates market expectations may already embed substantial recovery, leaving valuation/execution interpretation to Alpha.

unknowns.unknown: Current utilization and incremental return on the new 300mm capacity remain unquantified by these sources.
Current valuation and peer-relative expectations remain Alpha underwriting responsibilities.

recommendation: Reuse these two materially independent origins to construct source-addressed underwriting, risk and data-confidence evidence; do not infer a numeric score from Scout evidence alone.
